title: A curved spring warmth response of US lilac leaf-to-bloom gaps was uncertain in four samples from 1965 to 2008
abstract: We tested whether the response of the time from first leaf to first bloom changed with spring warmth. Four US lilac region and period samples used 5,715 paired plant-years from 1965 to 2008. Models had plant and year effects, winter temperature, and linear and squared spring temperature terms. The four squared-term estimates ranged from -0.250 to -0.124 days per C squared. All four intervals included zero after correction for four tests. March-April checks gave negative intervals in both early samples, but these results did not repeat in the later samples. The data do not establish a common curved response. Unknown visits, selected long records, different lilac types by region, coarse monthly weather, and approximate cluster intervals limit inference. This is a seasonal weather test. It does not measure daily extremes, pollution, community diversity, or a causal climate-change effect. The package contains a paired panel, source hashes, code, all results, a figure, and independent coefficient checks.

display.caption: Squared spring-temperature terms in four samples. Intervals use state and year clusters and a correction for four tests.
